name: Olive Tree
grown_as: An evergreen Mediterranean tree, in Britain usually kept in a large pot or a warm, sheltered spot. William's variety is not known; varieties differ mostly in fruit size.
habit: A small evergreen tree with a dense rounded head of silvery-grey foliage, 1.5 to 4 m in a garden. Trunk smooth and grey when young, later gnarled and twisted. Fine, square-ish young twigs.

leaf.arrangement: Opposite, in pairs up the twig
leaf.outline: Long and narrow, lance-shaped, 3 to 8 cm long and 1 to 1.5 cm wide
leaf.tip: Pointed, ending in a tiny sharp point
leaf.veins: Only the midrib shows; side veins hidden
leaf.surface: Leathery and stiff; dull dark grey-green above, silvery-white beneath from tiny scales

flower.petals: Four, joined at the base into a very short tube, the lobes spreading flat
flower.centre: Two stamens with large yellow anthers standing up from the middle
flower.carried: In short, loose, branching sprays (panicles) of ten to thirty, from the leaf angles on last year's shoots, held out or up among the leaves
flower.size: 5 to 6 mm across; the spray 3 to 5 cm long
flower.season: June, earlier under glass; sweetly scented

fruit: A drupe: oval, 1 to 3 cm, smooth and shiny, green at first, ripening through purple to black. Hangs on a short stalk, singly or a few together, among the leaves. Rarely ripens fully outdoors in Britain. Fruit set: tiny green ovals on the old flower sprays, most of which drop.
seedling: Not drawn: grown as bought plants

leaf: long narrow leaf with a smooth edge, no teeth
bloom: a tiny flower with four creamy-white lobes
two yellow stamens standing up from the middle
young: a small grey trunk with a head of twigs
narrow silver-grey leaves in opposite pairs
growing: a rounded evergreen head of narrow silvery leaves
flower: small branching sprays of tiny cream flowers from the leaf angles
set: small green olives on the old flower sprays
crop: oval olives, green, purple and black together, hanging on short stalks

look_alikes: Sea buckthorn and Elaeagnus have narrow silvery leaves but set alternately, with orange or silvery berries. Silver willow leaves are alternate and toothed. Phillyrea, a relative, has darker, glossier, often toothed leaves.
